title: Auto-triage eval regressions with contextual grouping and adaptive suppression for Slack/PagerDuty
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem: The current evals-alerting pipeline surfaces many individual regression signals (score drops, prompt-level failures, output skew) as separate notifications. This generates noisy Slack threads and duplicate PagerDuty triggers during config or model rollouts. Teams spend time triaging repeated signals that stem from the same root cause (e.g., a prompt set change, a model variant rollout, or a quantization profile adjustment).

This ticket proposes an auto-triage layer in the Console that groups related eval regressions by change context (model/config diff metadata, affected prompt subsets, and time window), applies adaptive suppression rules for noise reduction, and routes consolidated incidents to the appropriate Slack channel and PagerDuty escalation policy. The goal is to ensure on-call and product teams see actionable, de-duplicated incidents with enough context to decide next steps without losing fidelity for audit and postmortem use cases.
background:
Current behaviour: 1) Every eval threshold breach emits an alert. 2) Alerts are sent to static Slack channels and sometimes escalate to PagerDuty if a threshold is severe. 3) No consistent grouping by deployment metadata; separate alerts for related failures flood channels during rollouts.

Why this matters: As Dedicated and Private customers adopt more aggressive rollout strategies (canary + fast ramp), the volume of correlated eval signals increases. We need an automated way to: correlate signals, suppress duplicates intelligently, keep critical PagerDuty paths reserved for true incidents, and provide concise, reproducible context in Console and messages.
goals: Group related eval regressions originating from the same config/model change into a single consolidated incident
Provide enriched context (diff links, failing prompt examples, affected metrics) in the Slack/PagerDuty payload
Apply adaptive suppression to reduce alert noise by at least 50% while preserving high-severity escalations
Expose a per-project control in Console to tune grouping sensitivity and suppression windows
success_metrics: % reduction in unique Slack alert threads for eval regressions (target: 50% decrease)
False-negative rate for escalations remains < 5% compared to current baseline
Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for grouped incidents <= current MTTA (no regression)
Adoption: 80% of teams opt into auto-triage within 8 weeks of launch
assumptions: Eval events include structured metadata linking the event to a change: model_id, version, config_sha, rollout_id
Evaluation pipeline can emit hashes of failing prompt clusters to aid grouping
Teams can opt-out per project for conservative workflows (e.g., regulated customers)
PagerDuty integration supports dedup keys and custom payload fields to attach grouped incident context
acceptance_criteria: Console shows a "Grouped Incidents" view for eval regressions with links to the originating change (model/config) and failing prompt examples
Slack notifications for grouped incidents include: title, severity, link to Console incident page, top 3 failing prompts, change metadata, and a collapse summary
PagerDuty triggers use a stable dedup key per grouped incident and contain the grouped summary and link
Admin controls in Console to configure grouping sensitivity (low/medium/high) and suppression window (minutes/hours)
Manual validation: runhouse of synthetic rollout that previously produced 25 separate alerts now produces 3 grouped incidents; team confirms signal fidelity
Audit logs contain the original individual eval events for compliance and postmortem
notes: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting - alignment on goals and proposed grouping signals (config_sha, rollout_id, model_version). Action: ENG to prototype grouping keys.

2026-03-05: ENG spike completed - prototype groups events by (rollout_id + failing_prompt_cluster). First-pass shows 40% reduction in test noise. Action: refine prompt clustering to reduce false grouping.
2026-03-08: Design review - Diego recommended a collapsed card UI for grouped incidents with expand for raw events. Suggested adding 'why grouped' tooltip for transparency.
2026-03-10: Security review requested for PagerDuty dedup keys and possible information leakage in Slack payloads. Action: redact customer identifiers; include safe links that require Console auth.
2026-03-12: PM review - set target suppression default to 30 minutes for medium sensitivity. Decision: expose sensitivity slider in project settings.
Next steps: implement server-side grouping hook, build Slack/PagerDuty payload templates, and ship alpha to two internal teams for validation.
